 Dear Mr. Gardner, 
 The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of 
 five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  AES  Clean  Energy  LLC  (AES)  on  two 
 privately-owned  parcels  approximately  13.8  and  18.8  miles  south-southwest  of  Joseph  City, 
 Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the  Department’s  understanding  that 
 AES’s  proposed  installation  of  MET  towers  is  likely  part  of  a  larger  project  to  explore  and 
 potentially develop wind resources in this area. 
 Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona 
 Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust 
 responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the 
 Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for 
 safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly, 
 the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the 
 state’s  economic  growth  needs  and  opportunities  to  develop  renewable  energy  locations.  The 
 Department  recognizes  that  appropriate  coordination,  proper  planning,  and  voluntary 
 implementation  of  best  management  practices  allow  projects  to  be  developed  that  avoid, 
 minimize, or mitigate potential impacts to wildlife habitat and populations. 
 The  Department  supports  the  development  of  wind  energy  as  a  source  of  clean  and  renewable 
 energy  and  believes  that  with  proper  placement  and  planning  the  benefits  of  wind  energy 
 outweigh  potential  negative  effects  to  wildlife  populations.  As  identified  in  the  Department's 
 Guidelines  for  Reducing  Impacts  to  Wildlife  for  Wind  Energy  Development  in  Arizona 1
 (  Guidelines  ),  primary  concerns  with  MET  towers  are  the  potential  for  avian  and  bats  mortality 
 due  to  collisions  with  tower  guy-wires.  The  Department  appreciates  AES’s  implementation  of 
 the  Department's  guidelines  to  minimize  risk  to  our  pilots  engaged  in  low-altitude  wildlife  survey 
 flights  and  would  like  to  be  able  to  incorporate  the  GPS  coordinates  of  all  final  met  tower 
 locations  into  a  database  our  pilots  use  to  avoid  hazards.  Therefore,  the  Department  requests  that

 ndGuidelinesOctober2012.pdf

13-2022 approving/denying a Special Use Permit to construct and operate a 60 meter (approx. 197
foot) meteorological tower on APN # 111-04-001A, a portion of Township 15 North, Range 18
East, Section 23 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian.
Background:
The proposed project is a 60 meter (approx. 197 foot) meteorological tower with a requested
operation period of 60 months.  The meteorological tower will be outfitted with instrumentation
for the temporary purpose of resource assessment, to support the development of a potential wind
project.
None of the structures and equipment on the site will be permanent.  Once site usage has
terminated, all of these structures and equipment will be removed, and the site will be restored to
previous conditions.
This item was unanimously recommended for approval at the Planning and Zoning Commission
meeting held on March 17th, 2022, subject to the conditions outlined in the Staff Report and
Resolution for Approval.  These conditions include condition 13, relating to the expiry of the
Special Use Permit for this meteorological tower, which was recommended as a condition to be
added by the Commission.
Recommendation: 
Staff and the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommend approval of the
Special Use Permit, subject to the conditions within the Staff Report.

BACKGROUND/PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The applicant is requesting Special Use Permits to allow for the construction and operation of two, 60 
meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological tower for a period of 24 months.  One tower will be 
located on APN 111-08-001E and one on 111-04-001A.  The towers will be constructed of guyed steel 
monopole structure and installed on approximately 0.03 -acre pads, utilizing approximately 2 acres in 
space each when including the area encompassing guy-wires. 
 
None of the structures and equipment on the site will be permanent and will be removed from the site 
once usage has terminated.  The site will be required to be restored to the pre -disturbed/native state to 
the greatest extent possible upon completion of the usage of the meteorological tower. 
 
The applicant has reached out to the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding their proposals.  In 
a letter dated January 12th, 2022, the Game and Fish Department noted the following: 
 
“As identified in the Department’s Guidelines for Reducing Impacts to Wildlife for Wind Energy 
Development in Arizona (Guidelines), primary concerns with MET towers are the potential for avian 
and bats mortality due to collisions with tower guy -wires.  The Department appreciates AES’s 
implementation of the Department’s guidelines to minimize risk to our pilots engaged in low -altitude 
wildlife survey flights and would like to be able to incorporate the GPS coordinates of all final met 
tower locations into a database our pilots use to avoid hazards.  Therefore, the Department requests that 
AES provide the coordinates of the MET towers and notify the Department when the towers are erected 
and when they are taken down, so the database is up to date.” 
 
Conditions related to the Arizona Game and Fish Department have been included in the same  manner 
as previously approved projects. 
 
The last twelve (12) MET towers and MET tower operation extensions have been granted Special Use 
Permits by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors without any requirements related to expiry/renewal 
of Special Use Permits. 
 
At the Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing held on Thursday, March 17th, 2022 the Planning and 
Zoning Commission voted 5-0 to recommend approval of both of these Special Use Permits, subject to 
the conditions recommended by Staff, with the addition of the following condition: 
 
“The rights granted herein shall expire either sixty months (5 years) from the erection and Certificate 
of Occupancy of this tower or 72 months (six years) from the date of the Board of Supervisors approval, 
whichever comes first, unless an extension is granted by the Board of Supervisors.  Application for an 
extension shall be made no later than ninety days before the date of expiration.  If timely application is 
made, the expiration shall be tolled until a final decision by the Board of Supervisors.”

West Camp Wind Farm – MET Towers Narrative-1 January 21, 2022 
Navajo County Special Use Permit Application 
Introduction 
West Camp Wind Farm, LLC (Applicant) is requesting a Special Use Permit from Navajo County to allow 
the construction and operation of two meteorological monitoring towers (MET towers) on privately owned 
parcels. The Applicant proposes to locate the MET towers approximately 13.8 and 18.8 miles south-
southwest of Joseph City, Arizona, on what is commonly known as the Aztec Land and Cattle Company 
Ranch (Ranch) in unincorporated Navajo County, Arizona. The MET towers are intended to observe and 
record meteorological conditions to inform a future proposed electrical generation project on the Ranch. 
Description of the Applicant  
West Camp Wind Farm, LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of AES Clean Energy (AES). AES is the 
majority-owned United States renewable energy development business of The AES Corporation, a Fortune 
500 company that generates and distributes electrical power worldwide. Headquartered in Arlington, 
Virginia, The AES Corporation holds assets totaling over $35 billion. It is one of the world's leading power 
companies, generating and distributing electric power in 15 countries and employing 10,500 people. 
Based in Salt Lake City, Utah, and Louisville, Colorado, AES designs, builds, and operates solar, wind, and 
energy storage projects. Generation capacity of the systems owned and/or operated under AES totals over 3 
gigawatts (GW) across the United States, with another 1+ GW under construction. In addition, AES has a 
contracted renewable project backlog that includes over 3 GW.  
Description of the Project 
The Applicant is proposing to locate the MET towers on two parcels owned by the Aztec Land and Cattle 
Company, Ltd. (Figure 1). Parcel details are provided in Table 1. The parcels are zoned A-General, which is 
a rural land use designation for unincorporated areas of the County not specifically designated for any other 
zone classification. Within the A-General Zone, construction and operation of a MET tower is considered a 
specially permitted use, subject to issuance of a Special Use Permit.  
Table 1. MET Tower Location Information  
MET 
tower 
Assessor’s Parcel 
Number 
Latitude 
Longitude Location* Parcel Size 
1 111-08-001E 34.757511              
-110.388931    T16N R18E Section 25 3200.00 ac 
2 111-04-001A 34.685760         
-110.409950      T15N R18E Section 23 2913.36 ac 
* Gila and Salt River Baseline and Meridian 
The MET Towers would be constructed of a guyed steel monopole structure approximately 60 meters (197 
feet) tall. Each structure would be installed within a cleared, approximately 0.03-acre pad, and would occupy 
approximately 2 acres when including the area encompassing the guy-wires. For maximum safety, the towers 
would be painted orange and aviation white and include balls on the guy-wires. Project dimensions and 
details are shown in the site plan in Figure 2. Final design and engineering details of all structures will be 
provided in a future building permit application. The Applicant would micro-site the towers on site and the 
exact tower location could vary up to 250 feet from the location contained in this application.  
Construction and Operation Schedule and Phasing 
Installation of each MET Tower is anticipated to take 1 to 2 days, and the Applicant proposes to operate the 
MET Towers for up to approximately 5 years. Approximately three construction personnel would be 
required, and once operational the MET Tower would be operated remotely with a site visit every six months

<!-- page 769 -->
West Camp Wind Farm – MET Towers Narrative-2 January 21, 2022 
Navajo County Special Use Permit Application 
or as needed by one to two project personnel. Access to the MET tower locations would be from existing 
roads to the maximum extent possible. The MET tower locations would be accessed from the Highway 377 
that enters the ranch area south of Holbrook, Arizona (Figure 1). The MET tower locations would be 
accessed via existing roads as illustrated in Figure 1. 
Following project completion and the subsequent disassembly and removal of equipment, all disturbed areas 
would be graded to reasonably match the surrounding native areas, compacted to a similar state as existing 
native soils, and seeded with native vegetation. 
Legal Access to the Project Area 
The Applicant has lease agreements with the Aztec Land and Cattle Company, Ltd (property owner) for 
construction and operation of the MET towers. A signed owner affidavit is submitted with the Special Use 
Permit Application. 
The existing access road to the proposed MET Tower sites crosses Arizona State Trust and Bureau of Land 
Management (BLM) lands, as well as property owned by the Aztec Land and Cattle Company, Ltd (see 
Figure 1). The Applicant is currently in the process of applying for a Special Land Use Permit (SLUP) and 
will update the County regarding the application progress at the Planning and Zoning hearing.  
Community Outreach 
The Applicant provided notice of the project to identified stakeholders through the use of project 
informational mailings sent to the Arizona Game and Fish Department (AGFD) and ASLD on December 14, 
2021. The mailings described the project and provided methods (telephone, email, mail) and project contact 
information through which stakeholders could provide comments or ask questions about the project. There 
are no additional private property holders other than the Aztec Land and Cattle Company in the vicinity of 
the proposed MET Towers.  
The Applicant received one comment letter from the AGFD on January 12, 2022 (Attachment A). The letter 
requests that the Applicant provide the coordinates of the MET towers to the AGFD (which the Applicant 
has done) and notify the department when the towers are erected and when they are taken down so the 
database used by AGFD pilots to avoid hazards is up to date. No further public input has been received.  
Relationship to Surrounding Properties (ownership, zoning, 
uses, etc.) 
Property in the project vicinity consists of a checkerboard of private land, Arizona State Trust land managed 
by the ASLD, and federal land managed by the BLM. The private land in the project vicinity is owned and 
ranched by Aztec Land and Cattle Company, Ltd. Zoning of the surrounding private property is A-General. 
Land uses in and around the project area consist predominantly of livestock grazing and related ranching 
activities. The nearest residences to the proposed MET towers are located approximately 5.4  miles west of 
MET tower #1 and 5.7 miles southwest of MET tower #2. 
Three existing, county-permitted MET towers are located in the project vicinity. One is in T16N R18E 
Section 20, approximately 4 miles west of proposed MET tower #1. The second is in T15N R18E Section 9, 
approximately 2.7 miles northwest of proposed MET tower #2. The third is in T15N R17E, approximately 
4.6 miles west of proposed MET tower #2. The three existing towers were originally permitted by Navajo 
County to Invenergy, a renewable energy firm unaffiliated with the Applicant.

<!-- page 770 -->
West Camp Wind Farm – MET Towers Narrative-3 January 21, 2022 
Navajo County Special Use Permit Application 
Compliance with Navajo County Comprehensive Plan 
The proposed project complies with Navajo County’s Comprehensive Plan and does not have incompatibility 
issues with other permissible uses in the zoning district.  
The proposed project is also consistent with the Aztec Area Plan (Plan), which was developed in 2011 as a 
guide for the future development of a 228,040-acre property owned by the Aztec Land and Cattle Company, 
Limited, Aztec Land Company, LLC, and Aztec Despain Ranch LLC. To effectively plan for the future 
growth of the Aztec property, the Plan was prepared in accordance with Section 1.6 of the Navajo County 
Comprehensive Plan. The proposed MET towers are in the Plan’s West Camp planning area, portions of 
which are described in the Plan as having “the potential for wind energy production facilities.”  
Erecting and operating MET towers is a first step in assessing the quality of onsite wind resources and 
informing a future proposed renewable energy generation project, which would be a significant generator of 
economic and environmental benefits for Navajo County. The Applicant recognizes that approval of the 
MET towers does not imply future approval of wind turbines.

 The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of 
 five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  AES  Clean  Energy  LLC  (AES)  on  two 
 privately-owned  parcels  approximately  13.8  and  18.8  miles  south-southwest  of  Joseph  City, 
 Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the  Department’s  understanding  that 
 AES’s  proposed  installation  of  MET  towers  is  likely  part  of  a  larger  project  to  explore  and 
 potentially develop wind resources in this area. 
 Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona 
 Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust 
 responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the 
 Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for 
 safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly, 
 the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the 
 state’s  economic  growth  needs  and  opportunities  to  develop  renewable  energy  locations.  The 
 Department  recognizes  that  appropriate  coordination,  proper  planning,  and  voluntary 
 implementation  of  best  management  practices  allow  projects  to  be  developed  that  avoid, 
 minimize, or mitigate potential impacts to wildlife habitat and populations. 
 The  Department  supports  the  development  of  wind  energy  as  a  source  of  clean  and  renewable 
 energy  and  believes  that  with  proper  placement  and  planning  the  benefits  of  wind  energy 
 outweigh  potential  negative  effects  to  wildlife  populations.  As  identified  in  the  Department's 
 Guidelines  for  Reducing  Impacts  to  Wildlife  for  Wind  Energy  Development  in  Arizona 1
 (  Guidelines  ),  primary  concerns  with  MET  towers  are  the  potential  for  avian  and  bats  mortality 
 due  to  collisions  with  tower  guy-wires.  The  Department  appreciates  AES’s  implementation  of 
 the  Department's  guidelines  to  minimize  risk  to  our  pilots  engaged  in  low-altitude  wildlife  survey 
 flights  and  would  like  to  be  able  to  incorporate  the  GPS  coordinates  of  all  final  met  tower 
 locations  into  a  database  our  pilots  use  to  avoid  hazards.  Therefore,  the  Department  requests  that

 The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of 
 five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  AES  Clean  Energy  LLC  (AES)  on  two 
 privately-owned  parcels  approximately  13.8  and  18.8  miles  south-southwest  of  Joseph  City, 
 Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the  Department’s  understanding  that 
 AES’s  proposed  installation  of  MET  towers  is  likely  part  of  a  larger  project  to  explore  and 
 potentially develop wind resources in this area. 
 Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona 
 Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust 
 responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the 
 Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for 
 safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly, 
 the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the
